description: Everything merges on its own once CI passes: the ruleset `protect main` requires the checks that build and test every image, and GitHub's auto-merge (platformAutomerge) holds the merge until they pass, which is why platformAutomerge stays on here although the shared preset turns it off.

The shared preset's weekly schedule is replaced by "at any time" because a Debian snapshot carries security fixes and cannot wait for Monday; its wait for a tick on the Dependency Dashboard before a major is lifted by the last rule.

customManagers.description: The snapshot of the debian archive the images are built at. snapshot.yml writes the newest snapshots, when they change a published image, to the snapshot-feed branch; this moves lock.json's debian_snapshots to it. The quote after debian keeps it off the debian-security line.
The snapshot of the debian-security archive the images are built at: the same feed branch, its own file, its own line in lock.json's debian_snapshots.
The factory's builder image, by tag and digest. It moves with the factory's .pyz in lock.json, in one pull request.

packageRules.description: Each Node.js image follows one LTS line: Renovate moves its version inside that major only. A new LTS line gets a new image by hand (DESIGN.md, section 3).
The factory's .pyz and its builder image move together: builder.ref changes in the same pull request (scripts/policy.py refuses a mismatch).
The snapshots of both Debian archives move in one pull request, replaced while it waits, and it merges like every other update once CI passes.
prBodyNotes: snapshot.yml found that these snapshots change a published image: a Debian upload (often a security fix) touched one of their packages.

packageRules.description: A major update opens at once and merges on its own once CI passes, as every update did here before the shared preset: the required checks build and test every image, and the weekly schedule is replaced by "at any time" because a Debian snapshot carries security fixes and cannot wait for Monday. This also covers a snapshot whose year moves its first version part. Node.js majors stay off through the node-version rule above, which sets enabled and so applies whatever the rules around it say.
